subsystems.name: Growth reactor
subsystems.role: grows diamond from a gas mixture onto a heated substrate.

subsystems.name: Seeds and substrates
subsystems.role: provide the crystal template the diamond copies.

subsystems.name: Grown diamond material
subsystems.role: the structural substance itself: pure, monocrystalline, extremely stiff and thermally conductive.

subsystems.name: Shaping and finishing
subsystems.role: cuts and polishes a material harder than any tool can be made from.

subsystems.name: Joining and sealing
subsystems.role: makes small plates into large load-bearing structures, the hardest problem of all.

subsystems.name: Assembly and integration
subsystems.role: turns plates into shells, frames and hulls.

buildSteps.title: Make or prepare the seed
buildSteps.detail: Either grow a centimetre-scale single-crystal diamond plate under high pressure and temperature to act as a seed, or deposit an iridium layer on an oxide buffer on a silicon wafer so diamond can grow as one continuous crystal rather than a mosaic of grains.

buildSteps.title: Grow diamond by chemical vapour deposition
buildSteps.detail: Seal the seed in a vacuum chamber, add hydrogen with a few percent methane at roughly 15–30 kPa, and strike a microwave plasma that heats the surface to about 700–1000 °C. Atomic hydrogen etches away graphite as fast as it forms, so only diamond is left behind. Growth is slow — fractions of a millimetre per day — so thick plates take days to weeks.

buildSteps.title: Control stress and defects
buildSteps.detail: Vary methane concentration, temperature and doping, and anneal the plate, to keep dislocations and internal stress low. A structure that fails early will fail because of a defect, not because of the average strength of diamond.

buildSteps.title: Separate the plate from its seed
buildSteps.detail: Laser-cut or etch away the seed or buffer stack, leaving a free-standing monocrystalline diamond plate. Reusable seeds would be essential for any affordable route.

buildSteps.title: Shape the plate
buildSteps.detail: Cut and etch the plate to the wanted form. Ordinary machining is impossible because nothing is harder than diamond; lasers, plasma and diamond grit do the work.

buildSteps.title: Join plates into large forms
buildSteps.detail: Build up a shell or a frame by diffusion bonding or brazing smaller plates under heat and pressure. Joints, thermal-expansion mismatch with metals, and diamond's brittleness are the limiting factors, so graded interlayers would be needed.

buildSteps.title: Integrate with the rest of the system
buildSteps.detail: Fit metal flanges, seals, feedthroughs, sensor windows and thermal straps, using compliant interfaces to avoid concentrating stress on the diamond.

buildSteps.title: Test and proof every part
buildSteps.detail: Subject parts to pressure cycling, thermal cycling and impact. Diamond fails suddenly rather than bending, so each component would need individual proof testing rather than statistical sampling.

prerequisites.why: plates of a few millimetres exist in laboratories and specialist suppliers, but growth is slow and expensive and not yet structural scale.
growing one continuous crystal over a large wafer, rather than many grains, is what would allow large flat components.
without strong, sealed joints you cannot make a vessel larger than a single grown plate, no matter how good the material.
diamond has outstanding hardness and stiffness but low fracture toughness, so it needs careful shape and support to survive impact and pressure cycling.
diamond oxidises in air from roughly 600 °C and reacts with carbide-forming metals, limiting the truly 'extreme' environments it can face.

pathway.milestone: CVD diamond deployed as coatings on cutting tools, as heat spreaders behind high-power electronics, as optical windows and as radiation detectors; the term 'diamondoid' borrowed from speculative molecular-nanotechnology writing
pathway.unlocks: a working industrial base in growing diamond films and shaping them.

pathway.milestone: centimetre-scale monocrystalline plates and diamond grown over larger non-diamond wafers at lower cost
pathway.unlocks: flat components big enough to matter structurally, and cheaper thermal and optical parts.

pathway.milestone: reliable bonding and sealing of diamond to itself and to metals
pathway.unlocks: the first load-bearing diamond assemblies — pressure housings, stiff frames, windows in thick walls.

pathway.milestone: demonstrator shells tested under external pressure and thermal cycling
pathway.unlocks: deep-sea or extreme-environment enclosures, if brittleness, joining and cost can all be beaten at once.
